oncall-bot: ALERT: High 5xx rate detected in ap-northeast-1 for service: inference-api (route /*). Error spike started ~5m ago. Pager invoked for user sarah (oncall).

sarah (oncall): I’m on it. Seeing a surge in 502/504 from edge -> nat. Dashboard: latency +50% and errors ~20% of requests. Customers reporting timeouts.

miguel (neteng): FWIW we had a terraforming change earlier in ap-northeast-1 at 04:12 UTC that touched route-table rtb-0a1b2c3d. Could be a route drift to a deleted ENI.

sarah (oncall): Checking route tables now.

alex (infra): paste: ```aws ec2 describe-route-tables --filters Name=tag:Name,Values=rtb-public-apne1 --query 'RouteTables[].Routes'``` getting mixed routes, one route points to i-0deadbeef (gone).

sarah (oncall): That would blackhole NAT egress for the subnet. Confirming traffic graphs -> all egress from subnet-0123 stopped at NAT.

natalie (support): Heads-up: two enterprise customers (acme-corp, finlytics) reported request failures starting ~04:17 UTC. Both on Dedicated clusters in ap-northeast-1.

miguel (neteng): Looking at cloudtrail: api:ReplaceRoute called by CI user terraform@redwood at 04:12 UTC for rtb-0a1b2c3d -> target set to eni-removed-123. Reason: automated rollout of new NAT pair config. Seems the ENI was later terminated by autoscaler, leaving route pointing at dead target.

sarah (oncall): Immediate mitigation: update route to point at nat-gw-standby (nat-0feedface) which is healthy in same AZ. Running: ```aws ec2 replace-route --route-table-id rtb-0a1b2c3d --destination-cidr-block 0.0.0.0/0 --nat-gateway-id nat-0feedface```

deploy-bot: deploy:route-fix-job started by sarah at 04:28 UTC. CI job id: 18392.

alex (infra): Applied. Route now points at nat-0feedface. Doing conntrack flush on border hosts and invalidating prefix cache.

sarah (oncall): Monitoring metrics... errors dropping, p95 latency trending down. Can we confirm customer hit rate recovering?

natalie (support): Support: Acme-corp reports partial recovery at 04:33 UTC. Finlytics still sees intermittent 504s. I’ll open a ticket and triage specific requests.

miguel (neteng): We should also check NACLs — the terraform change also adjusted NACL rules for the AZ. I see a deny rule that blocks ephemeral ports from internal subnets (rule 110). That was unintended. Running ```aws ec2 describe-network-acls --network-acl-ids acl-0badd00d```

alex (infra): Confirmed NACL rule 110 was added by CI job 1765. Temporarily reverted to previous NACL state (removed deny).

sarah (oncall): After both route and NACL fix, egress restored. Full recovery seen by 04:40 UTC. Posting incident page.

kevin (oncall-next): I’m taking the handoff. Current status: mitigated, customer impact limited to ~20 minutes for most, a subset had up to ~25-30m retry windows. Waiting for postmortem ownership.

miguel (neteng): Root cause: automated terraform rollout replaced route to an ENI that was concurrently terminated by autoscaling; CI change also accidentally touched NACLs causing ephemeral port blocks. Two unsafe concurrent changes in same window.

alex (infra): Temporary remediation: add pre-check in terraform plan to ensure NAT ENI exists/attached before ReplaceRoute, and gate NACL changes behind a manual approval for production AZs.

sarah (oncall): Action items assigned: miguel -> revert auto-route rollout flow + add existence check (P1). alex -> introduce NACL approval gating (P2). natalie -> customer comms package and summary (P2). kevin -> run incident review and postmortem doc (owner).

deploy-bot: incident:created id=INC-2026-1793, severity=2, owner=kevin.

natalie (support): Sending initial customer status email now: summary + ETA for longer-term fix.

kevin (oncall-next): Handoff ack. I’ll coordinate postmortem and schedule a 60-min blameless review at 10:00 UTC. Closing the pager for sarah. Thanks everyone. :thumbsup:

sarah (oncall): Thanks team. Logging timeline and artifacts (CloudTrail, route-table diffs, CI logs) to the ticket.

migratory-note: followups: add monitoring alert for route pointing at non-existent ENI, and a runbook step for immediate replace-route to standby NAT.

kevin (oncall-next): Last check 05:00 UTC: metrics stable, customer queues drained. Marking incident RESOLVED and moving to postmortem phase.

natalie (support): Support tickets opened for impacted customers; CS will follow up for SLA credit assessment.

sarah (oncall): Closing thread, will add the runbook PR and link to postmortem doc.
